Strategy: Level the bins. Prefer the bin whose residual is closest to the mean residual, keeping fill levels even across bins. This skips the tightest bin, preserving it for a future item that fits it, and the emptiest bin, preserving free space for a future big item, so ranking can differ from Best Fit whenever the mean bin is not the tightest. It may help by avoiding fragmentation, but may fail by stranding tight bins if later items are large.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    avg = sum(bins) / len(bins)
    return [-abs(r - avg) for r in bins]
```
